items.content_text: NATO Allies should come together to form a defence financing instrument that supplements national defence spending, improves companies’ access to affordable capital, and incentivises joint procurement.

items.title: Rosatom is a Military Supplier – Europe Must Treat It as Such
items.content_text: Despite its involvement in Russia’s nuclear and conventional weapons production, Rosatom continues to maintain access to European markets.

items.title: Four Years On: An Update on the Air War Over Ukraine
items.content_text: An established Ukrainian F-16 Fighter Wing and the overstretch of fighters and air defences on both sides by sustained long-range strike campaigns have changed the nature of the air war.

items.title: Assessing China’s Language on its Stance on Ukraine and Belarus
items.content_text: The country’s different use of ‘territorial-integrity’ is more than a simple diplomatic gesture, but rather a useful sign of its alignment.

items.title: Burnham’s Makerfield Test: Home Gains or Global Risks?
items.content_text: Burnham’s Makerfield Test will reshape UK foreign policy. But will it deliver real benefits at home, or risk isolationism and strained alliances abroad?

items.title: Recce-Strike Provides a Generational Opportunity to Refocus Air Power
items.content_text: Air forces should be advocates of land recce-strike, which can hold the close fight with organic support, freeing air capabilities for the missions that justify them.

items.title: Whose Job is it to Protect the International Financial System?
items.content_text: International financial centres have lessons to pass on about the role of professional services in combatting illicit finance and kleptocracy.

items.title: Episode 24: Can the Financial Action Taskforce Turn Standards into Results?
items.content_text: How can the global anti-financial-crime system become more inclusive, proportionate and effective in delivering meaningful results?

items.title: Losing Control of the West’s Longstanding Interests in Seychelles
items.content_text: A democratic and well-functioning international financial centre that has benefited from Western support, Seychelles seems to now be choosing its friends elsewhere.

items.title: Prince Philip Lecture 2026: On Science and National Security
items.content_text: This year's lecture explores the significance of national security and defence skills, and the role of universities in educating the next generation of engineers and scientists.

items.title: RUSI Reflects: Andy Burnham's Geopolitical Priorities as New UK Prime Minister
items.content_text: With Andy Burnham set to become the next UK prime minister, RUSI's new director of international security evaluates the new leader's most pressing geopolitical priorities.
